name: King of Aphek
overview: The King of Aphek was a male ruler known primarily as one of the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua during the conquest of Canaan. His tribal affiliation and other personal details are not recorded in Scripture. This title identifies him as the sovereign over the city of Aphek, a significant location during the Israelite campaigns.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Aphek' straightforwardly denotes his rule over the city of Aphek. The name itself is a direct designation without additional given meaning or divine attribution, as noted in Joshua 12:18.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships or personal connections for the King of Aphek beyond his identification as a defeated king in Joshua 12:18. No further relational details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Aphek holds significance as part of the broader narrative of Israel's divinely guided conquest under Joshua. His defeat, alongside thirty other kings, marks the fulfillment of God's promise to give the land of Canaan to Israel. This victory demonstrates God's sovereignty and faithfulness in establishing His people in the Promised Land.
